title: 'Kuch Toh Log Kahenge': Ranbir Kapoor Shrugs Off Ramayana Trolling Before Release
excerpt: Days before Ramayana Part 1 opens in theatres, Ranbir Kapoor told 18,000 students that online trolling does not bother him and that the opinions of people who value his intentions matter most.
body:
• Ranbir Kapoor has answered the online trolling around Ramayana by invoking the Kishore Kumar classic "Kuch Toh Log Kahenge" — people will always talk.
  • Speaking with more than 18,000 students, he said what matters is the people who care about his work, his intentions and his kindness.
  • Ramayana, Nitesh Tiwari's two-part Hindi-language epic, opens in theatres on November 5, with Ranbir as Ram, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana.
  • Composer AR Rahman had earlier responded in similar terms when the film's songs drew criticism online.

Two days before the biggest release of his career, Ranbir Kapoor has given his answer to the trolls: a 1972 Kishore Kumar song. Kapoor, who plays Lord Ram in Nitesh Tiwari's two-part Ramayana, said he chooses not to be bothered by the online criticism that has followed the Hindi-language film's casting, music and visual effects, and that what matters to him is the support of people who understand his work and intentions. "I think what is relevant today is also the beauty of trolling online," he said, in remarks reported by BharaTimes. "It goes back to the old song, 'Kuch toh log kahenge, logon ka kaam hai kehna.' I think that's the great philosophy to actually follow. You don't get bothered by what people are saying."

What he told the students

Kapoor made the remarks during a recent interaction with more than 18,000 students from across the country, at an IIMUN event, according to Zoom's report. His message was aimed as much at the students as at his critics: do not let the noise decide anything. "Don't let the noise bother you. If your intentions are right and your hard work and dedication are honest, let your work do the talking," he said.

"What matters is the people. People who care for you, your work, intention, kindness, and I guess that's what matters the most."

— Ranbir Kapoor

Why the film has been under fire

The scrutiny has run on several tracks. Social media users have questioned Kapoor's casting as Ram and debated the film's VFX and music — a reaction amplified by the scale being promised: a reported budget of approximately ₹4,000 crore, MensXP noted, as promised by producer Namit Malhotra. Kapoor also faced a separate round of criticism after a slip of the tongue at a Ramayana event in Kolkata during Dussehra, for which he later apologised in Chennai, BharaTimes reported. He is not the only member of the production pushing back. Co-star Yash, who plays Ravana, urged audiences at a Hyderabad event to approach the film with an open mind rather than fixating on minor technical critiques, Zoom reported; and composer AR Rahman, asked about the criticism of the songs, said the team had done so much filtration and iteration that there was no energy left to look at feedback — a response we covered in our report on Rahman's remarks.

The film, and how to watch it

Ramayana is a two-part adaptation of the epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. Ranbir Kapoor leads as Ram, with Sai Pallavi as Sita, Ravi Dubey as Lakshman, Yash as Ravana and Sunny Deol as Hanuman. The first instalment opens in theatres on Thursday, November 5, 2026, with the second part expected in 2027. For diaspora audiences, the practical point is simple: this is a theatrical release first, and Kapoor's parting message before opening day is that the verdict he cares about belongs to the people who show up — not the timeline. The critics, for their part, have already had an early say in our roundup of the first reviews.
